ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the left side of the figure is a conjugated unsaturated aldehyde fragment bearing two R substituents, with an aldehyde group C(=O)H at the upper right end; at the lower right there is an enamine/amine fragment containing HN and bearing an R substituent. The curved arrows show the π electrons of the carbonyl C=O moving toward the oxygen atom, while the adjacent conjugated π bond migrates, and the enamine fragment connected to nitrogen participates in forming an N=C structure. Reasoning: After stepwise rearrangement of electrons according to the arrows, the original carbonyl oxygen gains a negative charge and becomes [O-], and a new C=C forms between the original carbonyl carbon and the adjacent carbon; the nitrogen fragment is represented as /N=C\C([H])[*] and is connected to the substituted carbon, while the remaining R substituents are represented by [*]. Therefore the rearranged molecular state corresponds to the SMILES [*]/C(C(/N=C\C([H])[*])C[*])=C/[O-].

method.method_draft: First describe the image structure: a substituted alpha,beta-unsaturated aldehyde is conjugated to an amine/enamine fragment, with arrows pushing the carbonyl pi electrons onto oxygen and shifting the neighboring pi system. Apply each arrow once: convert the C=O into C–O−, create the new alkene between the former carbonyl carbon and the adjacent carbon, and represent the nitrogen-containing fragment as /N=C\C([H])[*] attached to the substituted carbon. Then write the resulting atom connectivity with wildcard R groups as [*]/C(C(/N=C\C([H])[*])C[*])=C/[O-].
